narrative: Today's active-theme highlights span connectivity, climate response, and behavioural plasticity across taxa. In Landscape Ecology, an India-wide analysis of tiger, leopard, dhole, elephant and gaur habitat selection pinpointed connectivity pinch points concentrated outside protected areas, flagging protected-area-agriculture interfaces as priorities for large-mammal corridor restoration. Oikos synthesised evidence on the fate of Europe's mountain flora under warming, contrasting compositional turnover against the buffering effect of long generation times and specialised life histories in cold-adapted plant assemblages. A global phylogenetic meta-analysis in Journal of Animal Ecology found consistent urban-associated behavioural shifts (greater boldness, aggression and exploration, especially in birds), while a companion study in the same journal linked increasingly impervious European territories to paler carotenoid-based plumage in great tits. On invasion biology, a 17-site common-garden experiment showed introduced Chinese populations of smooth cordgrass have evolved a distinct fast-growth, strong-defence trait syndrome relative to their native US range, evidence of rapid post-introduction evolution. In Conservation Biology, restoration of drained temperate fens recovered both specialist species and ecosystem function, though the pace of recovery still tracked the degree of prior hydrological alteration. On the methods front, three new Methods in Ecology and Evolution papers converged on making bioacoustic deep-learning classifiers more accessible and efficient, from an evolutionary frequency-band-selection algorithm to the open-source Bacpipe pipeline. Finally, in Journal of Animal Ecology, eighteen years of tracking eastern grey kangaroos found that most maternal and environmental drivers of individual reproductive success fail to scale up to population-level recruitment, with birth asynchrony proposed as a buffer against environmental variability.
